strengths: Presents a novel and highly practical task of lifelong 3D head avatar modeling from unstructured, in-the-wild photo collections, relaxing the traditional assumption of shape invariance across a person's lifespan.

Proposes a well-thought-out architecture (TimeWalker) that combines the benefits of 2D Gaussian Surfels (DNA-2DGS), an adaptive Neural Head Basis blending module (Dynamo) for compact trait learning, and a Defer-Warping strategy to enable high-quality mesh reconstruction.
Contributes a new large-scale dataset, TimeWalker-1.0, containing over 2.7 million frames of 40 celebrities over multiple lifestages, which serves as a valuable benchmark for the community.

Provides extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations under two distinct protocols, outperforming state-of-the-art momentary head avatar models and generative baselines in terms of rendering quality, identity preservation, and geometry.
weaknesses: The approach is heavily reliant on FLAME fitting as a geometry prior. Inaccurate FLAME tracking on noisy, unstructured, or extreme-expression in-the-wild images directly leads to rendering and geometric artifacts, particularly around the mouth and eyes.
Rendering quality degrades significantly for large-viewpoint angles (yaw > 45 degrees) due to the highly uneven and long-tailed viewpoint distributions typical of unstructured web image collections.
Disentanglement between lighting variations and actual lifestage/identity attributes is not yet fully perfected; interpolating the residual embeddings can occasionally cause slight identity shifts.
The training time is relatively high, taking 3 to 5 hours on an NVIDIA A100 GPU per individual, which limits real-time or instantaneous deployment scenarios.

strengths: Presents a novel and challenging formulation of constructing 3D head avatars across a person's lifelong scale using unstructured in-the-wild image collections.
Constructs and promises to open-source a comprehensive dataset, TimeWalker-1.0, containing 2.7 million frames across 40 celebrities, which is a valuable resource for the community.
The proposed Dynamic Neural Basis-Blending Module (Dynamo) successfully prunes inactive hashgrids to maintain a compact, reusable representation across lifestages.
Provides extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations, including comparison with NeRF, 3DGS, generative, and one-shot head avatar baselines.
weaknesses: The technical novelty is somewhat incremental, as the framework mainly combines existing components such as 2D Gaussian Surfels, FLAME parameters, and multi-resolution hashgrids.

Heavy reliance on FLAME preprocessing: fitting FLAME on diverse, in-the-wild historical images is highly error-prone. Inaccuracies in the FLAME template directly propagate to the avatar reconstruction and animation quality, as visible in the mouth and tongue artifacts.

Incomplete disentanglement of lifestage and lighting: as shown in Figure 13, modifying the residual embeddings (intended for lighting control) can unintendedly alter the perceived age or identity of the person.

The process of defining and partitioning 'lifestages' is somewhat ambiguous. The transition between lifestages is represented discretely, which may not naturally capture the continuous process of aging.

strengths: Novel and Practical Task Definition: The paper introduces the task of modeling lifelong 3D head avatars from unstructured, in-the-wild photo collections across decades, moving beyond the traditional assumption of shape invariance.

Solid Technical Design: The proposed Dynamic Neural Basis-Blending Module (Dynamo) adaptively prunes inactive hashgrids to learn a compact representation, and DNA-2DGS successfully extends Gaussian Surfels with FLAME-guided deformation and Defer-Warping for dynamic mesh extraction.

Valuable Dataset Contribution: The paper presents TimeWalker-1.0, a large-scale, high-resolution dataset of 40 celebrities' lifelong collections containing over 2.7M individual frames with diverse age, head pose, and lighting variations.

Comprehensive Evaluation: Detailed quantitative and qualitative experiments on multiple protocols (1 vs 1 and 1 vs N) demonstrate superior performance in rendering quality (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) and identity preservation compared to state-of-the-art head avatar approaches.
weaknesses: Heavy Reliance on Parametric Prior: The framework is anchored on FLAME tracking. Inaccurate FLAME parameter estimation from noisy in-the-wild images can degrade reconstruction quality, and the model struggles to reconstruct fine-grained structures not captured by FLAME (e.g., the tongue).

Quality Degradation at Large Viewpoints: As shown in the qualitative results, the rendering quality degrades when the yaw angle exceeds 45 degrees, indicating limitations in handling highly imbalanced and unstructured view distributions.

Heuristic Pruning Threshold: The basis pruning mechanism in Dynamo relies on a preset threshold (kappa = 0.0001). The manuscript lacks a sensitivity analysis of how this threshold behaves across different identities with varying data qualities.

Paper Organization and Duplication: Table 3 and Table 8 are identical duplicates representing the same ablation study. Given that the main body of the manuscript is only 9 pages long, several critical ablation analyses and visualizations from the appendix could have been incorporated directly into the main text to make it more self-contained.
